string-array.name: help_fuel_level
string-array.item: How much fuel is in the tank, in percent.
Wanders on slopes, in turns and when accelerating: the fuel sloshes around.
Doesn\'t change although you\'re using fuel, or jumps for no reason: the tank level sensor.

string-array.name: help_l100
string-array.item: Instant consumption in liters per 100 km. Worked out from the hourly rate and speed, shown from 10 km/h.
Accelerating gives very large numbers for a moment.
If the ECU doesn\'t report fuel rate, it\'s estimated from MAF and is only approximate. Fill-ups are the best check: full tank, distance, liters.

string-array.name: help_lph
string-array.item: Consumption in liters per hour: how much fuel goes into the engine right now, whatever the speed.
Higher at cold idle than at warm idle.
If the name says \"from MAF\", it\'s worked out from air flow. With a dirty MAF it will be off too.

string-array.name: help_trim
string-array.item: How much fuel the ECU adds or takes away based on the front O2 sensors: short term plus long term trim. An inline engine has one bank. A V or boxer engine has two: bank 1 is the row with cylinder 1, bank 2 the other row. Which cylinders sit in which row depends on the maker: 1-3-5 and 2-4-6 on a GM V6, 1-2-3-4 and 5-6-7-8 on a Ford V8.
Within ±5 % is good, up to ±10 % is tolerable. On a V engine both banks should be about the same.

Positive means lean, the ECU is adding fuel: an air leak, dirty MAF, weak fuel pump. Negative means rich: a leaking injector, EVAP purge. Codes P0171/P0174 are lean, P0172/P0175 rich. If only one bank moved, look at that row: intake, injector, O2 sensor. If both moved together, the cause is shared: MAF or fuel pressure.
